title: Your Mum's State Pension Is £22 From Being Taxed 😳👵 #shorts
description:
Your mum's full State Pension is £22 from being taxed.

The full new State Pension is £241.30 a week in 2026/27 (£12,547.60 a year), just £22.40 below the £12,570 tax-free Personal Allowance. Any rise above 0.18% takes it over the line, so next April's yearly rise could do it.

In 2016/17 the full new State Pension was £155.65 a week (£8,093.80 a year), nearly £3,000 below the £11,000 Personal Allowance. Since then the pension has gone up 55% under the triple lock (the highest of inflation, average earnings growth or 2.5%), while the tax-free allowance has been frozen at £12,570 since 2021 and stays there until 5 April 2031.

Cross that line with no other income and HMRC would normally send a Simple Assessment letter (a tax bill). But at Budget 2025 the government said pensioners whose only income is the basic or new State Pension (without extra amounts) won't have to pay that small amount of tax from 2027-28. Details are due at the Budget on 28 October 2026.

If she has a workplace or private pension too, the State Pension already counts towards her tax: HMRC usually collects it through that pension's tax code.

Sources: https://www.gov.uk/new-state-pension/what-youll-get · https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/benefit-and-pension-rates-2026-to-2027/proposed-benefit-and-pension-rates-2026-to-2027 · https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2016/227/contents/made · https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/tax-and-tax-credit-rates-and-thresholds-for-2016-17/tax-and-tax-credit-rates-and-thresholds-for-2016-17 · https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/rates-and-allowances-income-tax/income-tax-rates-and-allowances-current-and-past · https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/maintaining-income-tax-and-equivalent-national-insurance-contributions-thresholds-until-5-april-2031 · House of Commons Library, Taxation of state pension (CBP-10250): https://commonslibrary.parliament.uk/research-briefings/CBP-10250/ · https://taxconfident.campaign.gov.uk/tax-in-retirement/how-state-pension-works/

facts.how: 2016/17: first year of the new State Pension, full rate £155.65 a week
Personal Allowance £12,570 'the level it reached in 2021/22', frozen since; held to 5 April 2031
£22.40 ÷ £12,547.60 = 0.18%: any rise above this crosses the line
Budget 2025: from 2027-28, pensioners whose sole income is the basic or new State Pension won't pay small amounts of tax via Simple Assessment; details not yet published
With a workplace/private pension, HMRC changes that pension's tax code to include the State Pension and collects the tax through it

assumptions: 'Your mum' = anyone on the full new State Pension (State Pension age from 6 April 2016).
'Next April's rise could tip her over': any rise above 0.18% does; the triple lock's floor is 2.5% (a government commitment, not a legal floor). The April 2027 rate is not yet confirmed.
'Probably paying already': with a workplace pension above about £22 a year and no other allowances.
